answer: In NIST AI RMF 1.0, transparency and accountability are supported by training data provenance through the maintenance of records that document the origin of training data and how it was used. This documentation ensures data quality and enables third-party assessments, which are essential for understanding the outcomes of AI systems. By keeping track of how data were collected, prepared, labeled, and maintained, organizations can provide meaningful transparency about their AI systems. This transparency is crucial for accountability, as it allows stakeholders to trace decisions made by the AI system back to specific subsets of training data, thereby facilitating redress for any negative impacts caused by the system.
